title: Grain Marketing Contracts: Delivery Window Lengths and Extension Allowances
content:
Every contract under Grain Marketing Contracts carries a contracted delivery window, and every programme carries an allowance by which that window may be moved out without the contract being rewritten. Both are set by the programme, not by the contract.

## Catalogue of window terms

| Programme | Contracted delivery window (calendar days) | Extension allowance (calendar days) | Extension charge (USD per bushel) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spot Cash Delivery Ticket | 1 | 0 | 0.000 |
| Forward Cash Sale Contract | 30 | 15 | 0.025 |
| Basis Fixed Contract | 45 | 30 | 0.020 |
| Hedge-to-Arrive Contract | 60 | 30 | 0.020 |
| Delayed Price Agreement | 30 | 15 | 0.025 |
| Minimum Price Contract | 60 | 30 | 0.020 |
| Managed Accumulator Program | 90 | 45 | 0.015 |

The window length is the length of the standard contracted delivery period the programme carries. The extension allowance is the number of calendar days the last day of that window may be moved out to without the contract being rewritten, and the extension charge is what those bushels carry per bushel for the privilege.

## Worked illustration on hypothetical figures

Take a hypothetical Hedge-to-Arrive Contract of 20,000 bushels. Its contracted delivery window runs 60 calendar days, and the last day of that window may be moved out by as much as 30 further calendar days within the allowance the programme carries. The extension charge on that hypothetical contract is 0.020 per bushel, so 20,000 bushels carry four hundred dollars of extension charge. A hypothetical Spot Cash Delivery Ticket carries a one-day window, no extension allowance at all and no extension charge, so nothing on that programme is moved out.

## Basis answered

Where a member asks how far the last day of a Forward Cash Sale Contract may move, the answer is 15 calendar days, at 0.025 per bushel. Where they ask the same of a Managed Accumulator Program, the answer is 45 calendar days, at 0.015 per bushel.
